claims.text: A propylene-fueled i7 torch can be used for low-temperature ID-HVAF deposition of FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy bond coats.
Conventional high-temperature deposition methods produce FeCoNiCrAl bond coats with relatively high oxidation levels.
Conventional high-temperature deposition methods produce FeCoNiCrAl bond coats with microstructural defects.
Low-temperature ID-HVAF deposition reduces in situ oxidation relative to conventional high-temperature deposition.
Low-temperature ID-HVAF deposition reduces deposition-induced thermal stresses relative to conventional high-temperature deposition.
Reduced oxidation and thermal stress produce a denser FeCoNiCrAl coating microstructure.
Reduced oxidation and thermal stress lower the density of oxidation-induced defects in the bond coat.
Lower deposition temperature preserves the homogeneity of the FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy.
Preserving bond-coat homogeneity and reducing defects improves adhesion between the bond coat and subsequent coating layers.
Improved adhesion and reduced defects increase resistance to thermal cycling.
FeCoNiCrAl bond coats deposited by low-temperature ID-HVAF will have a statistically significant longer thermal-cycling lifetime than conventionally deposited bond coats.
FeCoNiCrAl bond coats deposited by low-temperature ID-HVAF will exhibit a statistically significant lower failure rate than conventionally deposited bond coats.
The durability benefit should persist only below service temperatures that trigger drastic phase changes.
The durability benefit should persist only while service oxidation remains within the protective capacity associated with the processing route.
The proposed effect is specific to FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy compositions and similar processing environments.
